answer: Co-located Time-Lock Attestation. Each identity must periodically answer a random timing challenge over a dedicated radio link while a hardware beacon measures signal round-trip delay to the microsecond scale. A single operator cannot simulate many independent physical locations behind one beacon, since relaying adds measurable jitter a prism of directional antennas still cannot hide. Passing grants an encrypted velvet credential valid only until the next summit round. Cost: one beacon plus distinct real location per identity, roughly $200 and setup labor each.
